blocks.x: Season demand sensing for agri-inputs, stockouts on key SKUs down 24% and obsolescence write-offs down 31%

An agri-input company: Agricultural operations live by the season: one wrong input decision or one cold-chain gap shows up in yield, quality or compliance. The Achala team started where that cost concentrates —. The baseline signed in week two made the cost visible in units the finance team already owns, and the engagement ran under the standard Achala charter — a named metric, a named control owner and gates that evidence every move.

The baseline season costed the guess: 9% stockouts on key SKUs during the application window, 7.4% obsolescence write-offs on shelf-life-limited product, and regional plans built on last season's shapes plus sales optimism.
Season timing shifts, rainfall, planting windows, were visible in weather and agronomy signals but never reached the forecast. Distribution planned for a season that no longer arrived on schedule.

We built the season sensing spine: weather, soil-moisture and cropping signals joined to dealer sell-through in one governed model, demand sensing producing regional forecasts with the season timing as an explicit variable, allocation to dealers rebalanced weekly through the window, and write-off risk priced per SKU per region so supply trades stockouts against obsolescence honestly. The season arrives when it arrives; the plan now knows that.
